# m4040: DEM3D Shear Cross-Section Convergence

## 1. Case Introduction

The DEM3D direct-shear specimen measures apparent shear modulus by ramping the top layer of a bonded block. The earlier static reference (docs/dem3d_shear_static_reference.md) closed the WITHHELD but left open: a shape-independent material shear modulus could not be extracted because the 9x5 to 21x21 trend was too short to separate a lateral free-surface boundary layer from measurement bias.

This study runs 18 square cross-sections (n=5..61) at fixed h/a=2 (nz=3), no fracture, linear elastic static equilibrium.

**Parameters:**
| quantity | value |
| --- | --- |
| lattice | simple-cubic + 12 edge + 8 body diagonals, a = 0.05 m |
| cross-section | n x n, n in {5,7,9,11,13,15,17,19,21,25,29,33,37,41,45,49,55,61} |
| height | nz=3, h/a=2 |
| bond stiffness | k = 2000 N/m |
| C44 closed form | 7k/(3a) = 93.333 kPa |
| solver | scipy.sparse equilibrium, reaction cross-checked by IceDEM3D.forces |

## 2. Method

1. Static equilibrium solve per size via static_direct_shear() - one sparse solve, boundary conditions match solver's (bottom fixed, top u_x prescribed, lateral free).
2. Bond census area A_eff removes affine definition bias exactly.
3. Boundary-layer fit d(n) = c1/n + c2/n^2 + c0, where c0 is the asymptotic bias (falsification test).
4. Surface lag profile at mid-layer binned by distance from lateral face.

## 3. Results

| n | particles | G_eff/C44 | deficit d | A_eff/A_nom |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5 | 75 | 0.68721 | 0.31279 | 0.70857 |
| 9 | 243 | 0.84572 | 0.15428 | 0.83245 |
| 13 | 507 | 0.89759 | 0.10241 | 0.88250 |
| 21 | 1323 | 0.93877 | 0.06123 | 0.92647 |
| 29 | 2523 | 0.95633 | 0.04367 | 0.94649 |
| 41 | 5043 | 0.96947 | 0.03053 | 0.96201 |
| 45 | 6075 | 0.97225 | 0.02775 | 0.96536 |
| 61 | 11163 | 0.97971 | 0.02029 | 0.97356 |

Boundary-layer fit:
- c1 = 1.1910, c2 = 1.8459
- RMS residual = 4.70e-4, max |residual| = 9.9e-4
- Asymptotic bias c0 = 1.01e-3, G_inf/C44 = 0.99899
- Observed order p = 1.936
- Predicted n for 3% gate: 41.2 (measured: first below 3% at n=45)

## 4. Figures

Convergence figure (cross_section_convergence.png) embedded in report.json:
- Left panel: G_eff/C44 vs 1/n with fitted law and 3% gate
- Right panel: boundary layer profile for n=17,41,61

## 5. Caveats

- nz=3 is load-bearing: taller blocks relax more; convergence statement only valid at h/a=2.
- Linear elastic only: no fracture, no contact, no rate.
- Cubic-symmetry lattice: C44 is affine constant of this bond network, not isotropic ice.
- Mode-II fracture energy remains NOT_SUPPORTED.

## 6. Error Table

| quantity | value | baseline | relative error | < 3%? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C44 closed form | 93.333 kPa | 7k/(3a) | exact | yes |
| affine traction on census area | - | C44*gamma | <=1e-5 | yes |
| extrapolated G_eff(inf)/C44 | 0.99899 | 1 | -0.10% | yes |
| measured G_eff/C44 at n=61 | 0.97971 | 1 | -2.03% | yes |
| measured G_eff/C44 at n=45 | 0.97225 | 1 | -2.78% | yes |
| boundary-layer law vs 18-point series | - | data | RMS 0.05% | yes |
| asymptotic bias c0 | 1.0e-3 | 0 | 0.10% of C44 | yes |

Verdict: The finite-size deficit is a boundary layer with vanishing asymptote (c0=0.10%), so C44=7k/(3a) is recoverable - by extrapolation to 0.1%, or direct measurement at n>=45 to <3%.

## 7. Reproduce

PYTHONPATH=src python scripts/audit_dem3d_shear_cross_section_convergence.py
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/test_dem3d_shear_cross_section_convergence.py tests/test_dem3d_shear_static_reference.py tests/test_dem3d_shear_specimen.py -q

All 27 tests pass.
